examples.en: The snake came closer, flicking its tongue.

examples.ko: 난로 불길이 널름거리는 걸 한참 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched the flames licking in the stove for a while.
The puppy waits for a treat, licking its lips.
The lizard flicked its tongue in and out, which was fascinating.
Flames began to lick up over the roof.
The baby sticking its tongue in and out is cute.

explain: 혀나 불길이 빠르게 나왔다 들어갔다 하는 모습에 써요. 작은말은 '날름거리다'예요. 물결이 크게 흔들리는 '너울거리다'와는 다른 말이니 헷갈리지 마세요.

phrases.en: The lizard is flicking its tongue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 혀를 계속 내밀었다 넣었다 하는 동작에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the tongue keeps going in and out.

phrases.en: The flickering flames grew bigger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불길이 빠르게 일렁이는 모습을 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes flames moving quickly and flickering.

phrases.en: The fire in the stove flickers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 지금 보이는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form for describing what you see right now.

explain_en: It describes a tongue or flames quickly darting out and back in. The smaller-sounding version is '날름거리다'. Don't confuse it with '너울거리다', which is about large, soft waving.

examples.en: I twirl spaghetti around my fork and eat it.

examples.ko: 아기가 이불을 돌돌 말고 자고 있어요.
examples.en: The baby is sleeping rolled up in the blanket.
I rolled up the poster and put it in the tube.

examples.ko: 머리카락을 손가락에 돌돌 감는 버릇이 있어요.
examples.en: I have a habit of twirling my hair around my finger.

examples.ko: 김밥 속을 넣고 김을 돌돌 말아 주세요.
examples.en: Put the filling in and roll up the seaweed, please.

examples.ko: 실을 돌돌 감아서 서랍에 넣어 두세요.
examples.en: Wind the thread up and put it in the drawer.

explain: 가늘거나 얇은 것을 둥글게 여러 번 마는 모양이에요. 보통 '말다', '감다'와 함께 써요. '둘둘'은 같은 모양이지만 더 크고 두툼한 것에 쓰는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I roll the gimbap ingredients up in seaweed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얇은 것을 둥글게 여러 번 마는 모양에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes rolling something thin round and round.

phrases.en: I wound my hair around my finger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가는 것을 어딘가에 여러 번 두르는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes winding something thin around something several times.

phrases.example: 추워서 담요를 둘둘 말고 앉아 있어요.
phrases.en: It's cold, so I'm sitting wrapped up in a blanket.
phrases.nuance_ko: '돌돌'보다 크고 두툼한 것에 쓰는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels like it's for bigger, thicker things than 돌돌.

explain_en: It describes thin or slim things being rolled or wound round several times. It usually goes with '말다' or '감다'. '둘둘' describes the same motion but feels more suited to bigger, thicker things.

examples.en: It was cold, so I wrapped myself up in the blanket and slept.
I wound the scarf around my neck several times.
I wrapped the gift up in newspaper.
I wound tissue around my hand and wiped it.
Please wind the rope around the stick.

examples.ko: 아이가 담요를 둘둘 말고 앉아 있어요.
examples.en: The child is sitting wrapped up in a blanket.

explain: 길거나 넓은 것을 여러 번 감거나 마는 모양이고, '말다', '감다', '싸다'와 잘 같이 써요. '돌돌'은 더 작고 가벼운 느낌이고, '둘둘'은 더 크고 두툼한 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I wrapped the gift up in newspaper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 겹 감싸서 포장할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when wrapping something in many layers.

phrases.en: The carpet is rolled up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말려 있는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the state of being rolled up.

phrases.en: I rolled up the poster and put it aside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종이나 천을 말아 둘 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for rolling paper or cloth and leaving it.

explain_en: It describes wrapping or rolling something long or wide several times, and goes well with '말다', '감다' and '싸다'. '돌돌' feels smaller and lighter, while '둘둘' feels bigger and thicker.

t90.ax: I wrapped the gift up in newspaper.

examples.ko: 분가를 하려면 먼저 집부터 구해야 해요.
examples.en: If you want to move out, you first need to find a place.
My older brother is preparing to move out this year.
Even after moving out, I visit my parents often.
What was your reason for deciding to move out?

examples.ko: 분가는 보통 결혼할 때 많이 해요.
examples.en: People usually move out of the family home when they get married.
The newlyweds got a small home when they moved out on their own.

explain: 결혼 같은 일로 부모님이나 큰집에서 나와 따로 살림을 차리는 것을 말해요. 그냥 '이사'와 달리 가족에서 독립해 새 가정을 이룬다는 느낌이 있어요. 요즘 일상에서는 '독립'이라는 말을 더 많이 쓰고, 반대로 다시 합치는 건 '합가'라고 해요.

phrases.en: My older brother will move out soon after getting married.
phrases.nuance_ko: '분가'에 '하다'를 붙여 동사처럼 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '하다' added to '분가' so it works like a verb.
phrases.en_equiv: to move out and set up one's own household

phrases.en: The couple is preparing to move out on their own.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집을 구하는 등 나갈 계획을 세울 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when planning to leave, such as looking for a home.

phrases.en: I became independent after getting a job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요즘 일상 대화에서는 '분가'보다 이 말을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is used more than '분가' in everyday talk these days.

explain_en: It means leaving your parents' or the main family's home, usually after marriage, to set up your own household. Unlike plain '이사' (moving), it carries the feeling of becoming a separate family. In daily talk '독립' is more common now, and the opposite, living together again, is '합가'.

t90.ax: What was your reason for deciding to move out?

examples.ko: 모기가 귀 옆에서 윙윙거려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: A mosquito buzzed next to my ear, so I couldn't sleep.
Bees are buzzing around the flowers.
The fan whirred all night.

examples.ko: 윙윙거리는 소리 때문에 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: I can't concentrate because of the buzzing sound.
A fly is buzzing around over the food.
I get annoyed every time a mosquito buzzes.

explain: 벌, 모기, 선풍기, 기계처럼 낮고 가늘게 이어지는 소리를 낼 때 써요. 귀에서 윙윙 소리가 나는 느낌을 말할 때도 '귀가 윙윙거려요'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The buzzing sound woke me up all night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 소리를 꾸미는 말이고 짜증 나는 느낌이 자주 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-는' form modifies a sound and often carries an annoyed feeling.

phrases.en: The refrigerator makes a humming sound.
phrases.nuance_ko: '윙윙' 뒤에 '소리가 나다'를 붙이면 더 쉽게 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '소리가 나다' after '윙윙' is a simpler way to say it.

phrases.en: A mosquito buzzes next to my ear.
phrases.nuance_ko: '윙윙거리다'와 뜻이 같고 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '윙윙거리다' and interchangeable.

explain_en: It describes the low, continuous sound made by bees, mosquitoes, fans and machines. It is also used for ringing in the ears, as in '귀가 윙윙거려요'.

examples.ko: 아기 이름 작명은 할머니께서 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother chose the baby's name for us.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 작명 센스가 정말 좋아요.
examples.en: This shop has a really great sense for naming things.
Naming is hard, so I've been agonizing over it for days.
We got the baby's name from a naming house.
We picked the puppy's name from a naming contest.

examples.ko: 게임 캐릭터 작명에 두 시간이나 걸렸어요.
examples.en: Naming my game character took a whole two hours.

explain: 사람 이름뿐 아니라 가게, 제품, 반려동물 이름을 지을 때도 써요. 일상에서는 '이름 짓기'라고도 하고, '작명 센스'는 이름을 재치 있게 잘 지었을 때 칭찬하는 말로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: This shop has a fun sense of naming.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이름을 재치 있게 지었을 때 칭찬하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compliment for a cleverly chosen name.

phrases.en: We left naming the baby to my grandfather.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이름 짓는 일을 다른 사람에게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when asking someone else to come up with a name.

phrases.en: Naming the puppy was the hardest part.
phrases.nuance_ko: '작명'과 같은 뜻의 쉬운 말로 일상에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy equivalent that's more common in daily speech.

explain_en: It is used not only for people's names but also for shops, products and pets. In everyday talk you can also say '이름 짓기'. '작명 센스' is a common way to praise someone for coming up with a clever name.

examples.en: I reorganized the order of the story and rewrote it.
We decided to rearrange the office seating.

examples.ko: 사건 현장을 재구성해 보니 단서가 보였어요.
examples.en: When we reconstructed the scene, clues appeared.

examples.ko: 수업 내용을 재구성한 자료를 나눠 줬어요.
examples.en: They handed out materials with the lesson content restructured.
The presentation order needs to be reorganized.
The reorganizing took a lot of time.

explain: 이미 있는 내용이나 구조를 다시 짜 맞춘다는 느낌이에요. 글, 수업 자료, 사건 설명 등에 두루 쓰고, 보통 '재구성하다' 형태로 말해요.

phrases.en: I reorganized the lesson content to make it easier.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자료나 글의 내용을 다시 짤 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when rearranging the content of materials or writing.

phrases.example: 이 책은 실제 사건을 바탕으로 재구성되었어요.
phrases.en: This book was reconstructed based on a real event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 하는 일이 아니라 결과를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a result rather than your own action.

phrases.example: 글이 재구성을 거쳐 훨씬 읽기 쉬워졌어요.
phrases.en: After being reorganized, the text became much easier to read.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다시 짜는 과정을 지나왔다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means something has gone through the process of being reorganized.

explain_en: It carries the feeling of putting existing content or structure together again. It is used broadly for writing, lesson materials and accounts of events, and is usually said as '재구성하다'.

t90.ax: The reorganizing took a lot of time.

examples.en: I changed the order of the presentation and reorganized the content.

examples.ko: 선생님이 수업 자료를 학생 수준에 맞게 재구성하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher reorganized the lesson materials to fit the students' level.

examples.ko: 이 글을 시간 순서대로 재구성해 볼까요?
examples.en: Shall we try rearranging this text in chronological order?

examples.ko: 사건 현장 사진으로 그날 상황을 재구성하고 있어요.
examples.en: They are reconstructing what happened that day using photos from the scene.

examples.ko: 소설을 영화로 재구성하면서 결말이 많이 달라졌어요.
examples.en: As the novel was reworked into a movie, the ending changed a lot.
Some suggested restructuring the department.

explain: 이미 있는 것을 순서나 구조를 바꿔서 새로 짜 맞출 때 써요. 글, 수업, 팀, 사건 과정 같은 말과 잘 어울려요. '다시 재구성하다'는 '재'가 겹쳐서 어색하니 '재구성하다'만 쓰세요.

phrases.en: I'll reorganize the text by changing the order.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 하겠다는 뜻을 말할 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Future-intent form for saying you will reorganize something.

phrases.en: The reorganized class material is much easier.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Modifier form placed before a noun.

phrases.en: The team was reorganized.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 하는 것이 아니라 바뀐 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Passive form describing the result of being reorganized.

explain_en: Use it when you take something that already exists and rearrange its order or structure into something new. It goes well with texts, lessons, teams and event reconstructions. '다시 재구성하다' repeats the idea of 'again' and sounds awkward, so just say '재구성하다'.

examples.ko: 글말과 입말은 쓰는 단어가 조금 달라요.
examples.en: Written and spoken language use slightly different words.

examples.ko: 이 표현은 글말에서만 쓰고 말할 때는 안 써요.
examples.en: This expression is only used in writing, not in speech.

examples.ko: 뉴스 기사는 대부분 글말로 쓰여 있어요.
examples.en: News articles are mostly written in written language.
Written language has longer and stiffer sentences than spoken language.

examples.ko: 외국인 학생들은 글말보다 입말이 더 어렵대요.
examples.en: I hear foreign students find spoken language harder than written language.
You have to use written language in letters or reports.

explain: 반대말은 '입말'이에요. 한자어로는 '문어'와 '구어'라고 하는데, '글말'과 '입말'은 순우리말이라 설명할 때 편하게 써요.

phrases.en: Written and spoken language use different expressions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말과 함께 짝으로 쓰는 가장 흔한 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form, paired with its opposite.

phrases.en: This word is usually used in writing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 표현이 글에서만 쓰인다고 설명할 때 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Good for explaining that an expression is used only in writing.

phrases.en: Written-style expressions appear a lot in the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: '글말'이 뒤의 명사를 꾸며서 표현의 종류를 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: 글말 modifies the noun to show the type of expression.

explain_en: The opposite is '입말' (spoken language). The Sino-Korean terms are '문어' and '구어', while '글말' and '입말' are native Korean words that are easy to use when explaining.

t90.ax: News articles are mostly written in written language.

examples.en: The word for 'pear', 'ship' and 'belly' is a homonym.

examples.ko: 한국어에는 동음이의어가 많아서 문맥을 보고 판단해야 해요.
examples.en: Korean has many homonyms, so you have to judge by context.

examples.ko: 동음이의어로 된 농담이 이해가 안 돼요.
examples.en: I don't get the joke that's built on a homonym.

examples.ko: 사전에서 동음이의어는 번호를 붙여 따로 정리해요.
examples.en: In a dictionary, homonyms are listed separately with numbers.
Try finding homonyms that sound the same, like the word for 'snow' and 'eye'.
This quiz is made up of questions that use homonyms.

explain: 소리와 모양은 같지만 서로 관련 없는 뜻을 가진 말이에요. 한 단어의 뜻이 넓어져 여러 뜻이 된 '다의어'와는 달라요. 사전에서는 보통 번호를 붙여 따로 실려요.

phrases.en: You have to tell homonyms apart by the context.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 같은 말의 뜻을 가려낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for figuring out which meaning of a same-sounding word is intended.

phrases.en: '눈' is a good example of a homonym.
phrases.nuance_ko: 설명할 때 어떤 단어가 그 예인지 말하며 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say which word is an example when explaining.

phrases.en: It's fun to make puns with homonyms.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 같은 말을 이용해 농담할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for jokes that play on same-sounding words.

explain_en: These are words with the same sound and spelling but unrelated meanings. They differ from '다의어' (polysemous words), where one word's meaning has branched out. Dictionaries usually list them separately with numbers.

examples.ko: 우리 반은 졸업할 때 문집을 만들었어요.
examples.en: Our class made an anthology when we graduated.
I was happy that my poem was published in the anthology.

examples.ko: 이 문집은 학생들이 직접 쓴 글을 모았어요.
examples.en: This anthology collects writing that the students wrote themselves.

examples.ko: 문집 표지는 미술 동아리 친구가 그렸어요.
examples.en: A friend from the art club drew the cover of the anthology.

examples.ko: 선생님이 우리 글을 엮어 문집으로 내셨어요.
examples.en: Our teacher gathered our writing and published it as an anthology.
Last year's anthology is still on the bookshelf.

explain: 학교나 동아리에서 학생들의 글을 모아 만든 책을 말할 때 자주 써요. 한 사람의 글을 모은 책에도 쓰지만, 일상에서는 졸업 문집처럼 함께 만든 책이 먼저 떠올라요. '시집'은 시만, '문집'은 여러 종류의 글을 모은 책이에요.

phrases.example: 졸업 문집에 친구들 글이 다 들어 있어요.
phrases.en: All my friends' writings are in the graduation anthology.
phrases.nuance_ko: 졸업할 때 함께 만드는 책을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the book made together at graduation.

phrases.example: 우리 동아리 문집이 다음 달에 나와요.
phrases.en: Our club's anthology comes out next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동아리 회원들의 글을 모은 책이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A book collecting the writings of club members.

phrases.en: I included a short essay in the anthology.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 글을 책에 넣을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The usual phrase for putting your own writing into a book.
phrases.en_equiv: to contribute writing to an anthology

explain_en: It is often used for a book of writing collected at a school or club. It can also mean one person's collected works, but in daily life people first think of a graduation anthology made together. '시집' holds only poems, while '문집' gathers many kinds of writing.

examples.en: I read this novel in the Korean translation.
The translation is easier than the original.
I found the English translation at the bookstore.
The title differs a little in each translation.

examples.ko: 번역본은 읽기는 쉽지만 느낌이 조금 달라요.
examples.en: A translation is easy to read, but the feel is a bit different.
My friend left notes in the translated copy.

explain: 번역하기 전의 글은 '원본'이나 '원서', 번역한 책은 번역본이에요. 외국어로 쓴 책은 보통 '원서'라고 불러요. '한국어판', '영어판'처럼 '판'을 붙여 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: English books are still hard, so I read the translation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원서 대신 번역된 책을 읽을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when reading a translated book instead of the original.

phrases.en: This book also has an English translation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에 언어 이름을 붙여 어떤 번역본인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the language name before it to say which translation.

phrases.en: The Korean edition of this book came out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 번역본과 비슷하지만 책으로 나온 판을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 번역본, but focuses on the published edition.

explain_en: The text before translation is 원본 or 원서, and the translated book is 번역본. A book in a foreign language is usually called 원서. People also say 한국어판 or 영어판 by adding 판.

t90.ax: I read this novel in the Korean translation.

examples.ko: 서점에서 영한 소사전을 한 권 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a small English-Korean dictionary at the bookstore.

examples.ko: 이 소사전은 작아서 가방에 넣고 다니기 좋아요.
examples.en: This pocket dictionary is small, so it's easy to carry in a bag.
This word is listed even in the small dictionary.
A travel mini dictionary is handy to have.
It's hard to find difficult words in a small dictionary.

examples.ko: 소사전 한 권이면 기초 단어는 충분해요.
examples.en: One small dictionary is enough for basic words.

explain: 크기가 작고 단어 수가 적은 사전이에요. 반대로 많은 단어를 실은 큰 사전은 '대사전'이라고 해요. 요즘은 종이 사전보다 앱이나 인터넷 사전을 많이 써서 '사전'이라고만 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.example: 여행 갈 때 휴대용 소사전을 챙겼어요.
phrases.en: I packed a portable mini dictionary for the trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들고 다니기 쉬운 작은 사전을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a small dictionary that is easy to carry.

phrases.en: I checked the word's meaning in a Korean-English mini dictionary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 언어 이름을 앞에 붙여 어떤 사전인지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the language pair in front to say what kind of dictionary it is.

phrases.en: I look up words I don't know in the dictionary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크기와 상관없이 쓰는 기본 말이라 일상 대화에서는 이게 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic word regardless of size, and more natural in daily conversation.

explain_en: It is a dictionary with a small size and fewer entries. The opposite, a large one with many entries, is a '대사전'. These days many people use apps or online dictionaries, so they often just say '사전'.
